themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Posting complaints exploded to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks — a 3900% spike with z-score of 14.74 — suggesting coordinated poster campaigns or enforcement gaps in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 5 Illegal Posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
311 data shows this is newest spike in the dataset (this week origin)
reporting_angles: Ground canvassing: are specific blocks blanketed with illegal posters (events, political, commercial)? Is there a pattern?
Source investigation: who is posting and why now? Political campaign, real estate, entertainment promotion?
Sanitation response: why did enforcement or removal capacity drop?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Dead Animal complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK compared to a 1.0 per-week baseline — a 500% increase with z-score 5.0 — potentially signaling a public health or pest control issue in the district.
evidence: 6 Dead Animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.0 indicates highly significant deviation
Spike emerged this week, no prior warning signal
reporting_angles: Verify locations: are dead animals concentrated in one area (park, waterfront, residential block) suggesting localized die-off or abuse?
Health angle: could spike indicate rodent outbreak, disease vector, or seasonal die-off?
City response: what is NYPD/Sanitation doing to investigate and clear carcasses? Speed of removal?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor Air Quality complaints doubled to 14 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 7.0 per week — a 100% jump with z-score 3.5 — coinciding with heat complaints (4,237 over 90 days) and suggesting building ventilation or cooling failures.
evidence: 14 Indoor Air Quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (100% increase)
Z-score of 3.5 marks statistically significant spike
Correlates with persistent Heat/Hot Water complaints (4,237 total over 90 days), suggesting systemic building issues
Recent fire escape violations cited in Inwood blaze (THE CITY, 5/14/2026) indicate neglected building conditions may extend to HVAC/ventilation
reporting_angles: Building-by-building audit: which properties are generating multiple air quality complaints? Are they the same landlords cited for fire code violations?
Tenant interviews: are residents experiencing mold, inadequate ventilation, or CO concerns alongside heat failures?
HPD enforcement: what violations are being issued for indoor air quality? How many repeat offenders?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling & Encampment Pressure
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK (220% above the 1.9 weekly baseline), while Encampment complaints peaked at 23 two weeks ago (411% above 4.5 baseline) — together indicating a growing street-level homelessness and social services crisis in Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: Panhandling: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (220% increase, z-score 3.54)
Encampments: 23 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.5 weekly average (411% increase, z-score 4.39)
Two distinct spikes (different timeframes) suggest sustained or rolling homelessness pressure, not one-time event
Community Board budget requests show repeated pleas for park safety staff and food assistance—long-running unmet needs
reporting_angles: Encampment mapping: where are the 23 reported camps? Parks, streets, transit hubs? Are they persistent or migrating?
Outreach gap: what NYC social services are (or aren't) reaching these populations? Why the sudden visibility?
Resident and merchant interviews: how are panhandling and encampments affecting foot traffic, sense of safety, business?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.1 per week — a 344% spike with z-score 3.32 — suggesting rapid deterioration of building infrastructure alongside the district's persistent heat, plumbing, and paint/plaster complaints.
evidence: 5 Elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% increase, z-score 3.32)
Emerges alongside Heat/Hot Water (4,237 complaints), Plumbing (1,050), and Paint/Plaster (1,076) — cluster suggests systematic building maintenance failures
Recent fire escape violations in Inwood blaze (THE CITY, 5/14/2026) demonstrate landlord negligence may be widespread across building systems
reporting_angles: Property analysis: which buildings have clustered elevator + heat + plumbing complaints? NYPD patterns of violations?
Tenant interviews: in elevator-out buildings, how are elderly and disabled residents accessing apartments? Are they trapped?
HPD enforcement: elevator violations carry fines and DOB compliance orders—are problem landlords repeat offenders facing escalation?
